edges.description: Glia-specific loss of NF155, the isoform affected in most patients, prevents paranodal junction formation, slows peripheral conduction and causes ataxia, paresis and degeneration of myelinated axons.
edges.limitations: The mice die before the third postnatal week, earlier than most patients, and the cerebral white matter and cognitive features of the human disease cannot be assessed.

edges.description: Loss of NF186 from Purkinje cells disrupts the axon initial segment, mislocalises sodium and potassium channels, and leads to Purkinje cell degeneration with cerebellar dysfunction.
edges.limitations: Deletion is restricted to Purkinje cells, whereas the patient splice variant removes full-length NF186 from all neurons.
